content.summary: Recommendations for lipid-lowering therapy in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) patients.
recommendations: Initiate PCSK9 inhibitor treatment during ACS hospitalization for patients not at LDL-C goal despite statin and ezetimibe therapy.
Re-evaluate lipid levels 4–6 weeks after each treatment or dose adjustment to assess goal attainment and safety.
If LDL-C goals are not achieved with maximum tolerated statin alone after 4–6 weeks following ACS, add ezetimibe.
Initiation of PCSK9 inhibitor treatment is recommended in patients who do not reach their LDL-C goal despite maximum tolerated statin and ezetimibe.
Icosapent ethyl 2 g b.i.d. can be used with a statin in patients with ACS and triglycerides 1.5–5.6 mmol/L (135–499 mg/dL) despite statin treatment.
content.monitoring: Lipid levels should be re-evaluated 4–6 weeks after treatment initiation or dose changes; therapeutic regimen adapted accordingly.
content.notes: Data show PCSK9 inhibitors are safe and effective in lowering LDL-C in patients hospitalized with ACS and can improve plaque phenotype and regression. An algorithm for lipid-lowering management in ACS patients is outlined in Figure 18.

Associated Conditions: Elevated LDL-C / failure to reach LDL-C goals despite statin and ezetimibe
Atherosclerotic plaque phenotype and plaque regression
genes.context: The guideline states that treatment with PCSK9 inhibitors has been shown to be safe and effective in lowering LDL-C in patients hospitalized with ACS and that initiation of PCSK9 inhibitor treatment is recommended during ACS hospitalization for patients not at their LDL-C goal despite statin and ezetimibe.
